title: Angevins
capsule: The Angevins as attested here represent the County of Anjou under the Plantagenet line during the mid-twelfth century, spanning the reigns of Fulk V (until 1129, when he departed for Jerusalem to become king) and his son Geoffrey V 'Plantagenet' (1129–1151). Geoffrey systematically conquered the Duchy of Normandy between 1141 and 1144, entering Rouen and receiving the ducal crown at the cathedral, while suppressing repeated baronial rebellions at home. His marriage to Empress Matilda in 1128 and the subsequent inheritance claim laid the groundwork for the Angevin Empire under their son Henry II, who became king of England in 1154. The county itself served as the dynastic core from which Plantagenet territorial ambitions across France and England radiated.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The county's core territory around Angers is well documented, but the precise extent of its fluctuating control over contested border lordships in this period is only approximately known.
